solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Outcast in revolt on the counter

indicators.note: going counter, against the usual direction, so the word for revolt is read backwards

parts.note: to revolt someone is to repel or disgust them

explanation.surface: A rebel caught up in an uprising, perhaps standing on a shop counter to address the crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the counter' turns REPEL round to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A person shunned by society is an outcast, the figurative sense of someone once isolated for disease.

clue.text: Writer reporting the song of an East Sussex town?

indicators.note: reporting means passing on by word of mouth, so we want what the phrase sounds like

parts.words: the song of an East Sussex town
parts.note: Lewes is the county town of East Sussex, in southern England, and a carol is a song

explanation.surface: A writer is said to be describing a local anthem of a small English town.
explanation.walkthrough: LEWES CAROL said out loud matches the pen name of the author of Alice in Wonderland. Lewes is a town in East Sussex, a county on England's south coast.
explanation.definitionFit: The pen name of Charles Dodgson, author of the Alice books, so he is a writer.

clue.text: River bird stopping short of the far north, perhaps?

parts.note: the Po is the great river of northern Italy

indicators.note: the bird's name stops short, losing its final letter

parts.note: the lark is a songbird

explanation.surface: A river bird halts its migration just before reaching the Arctic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' is there because the word covers the far south too.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes the regions round either pole, the far north being one example.

clue.text: Hiding in temple, raised seat drops from above

indicators.note: the reversed seat word hides, or wraps round, the next two pieces
in a down clue raised means read upwards, so the seat word is reversed

parts.note: the rear is the seat or bottom
a wat is a Buddhist temple in Thailand or Cambodia

explanation.surface: Someone sheltering in a temple sees a raised seat from which things drip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hiding' looks like the start of a concealed-word clue, but here the upturned seat simply wraps round the temple pieces. A wat is a temple in Thailand.
explanation.definitionFit: Water falling from the sky as rain is literally drops coming from overhead.

clue.text: Very dark stream, second to circle lake

parts.note: a jet is a stream of liquid or gas forced out

indicators.note: the word for second goes round the lake letter

parts.note: to second a motion is to back it
L is the standard abbreviation for lake on maps

explanation.surface: A gloomy stream, and a second one that loops round a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to circle' puts L inside BACK, giving BLACK.
explanation.definitionFit: Black like the gemstone jet, the deepest black, so extremely dark in colour.

clue.text: Dance understood to be a puzzle

parts.note: a jig is a lively folk dance
I saw means I understood

explanation.surface: A dance someone grasped turns out to be a puzzle.
explanation.definitionFit: A picture cut into interlocking pieces to be reassembled is a kind of puzzle.

clue.text: I'm going to impersonate flipping lion and duck!

indicators.note: flipping turns the word for impersonate over, so it reads backwards

parts.note: to do someone is to impersonate them
Leo is the lion of the zodiac
a duck is a zero score in cricket, the letter O

explanation.surface: Someone announces a plan to do a lion and duck impression, with the mild oath flipping.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition stops at 'going': the 'to' that follows is a separate piece, and 'flipping' acts only on the impersonate word.
explanation.definitionFit: A jaunty old British way of saying goodbye, the same as announcing one's departure.

clue.text: Old party leader in retreat, a sign

parts.note: Lib stands for the Liberals, a former British political party

indicators.note: the leader in a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A former party leader, now retired, makes a gesture.
explanation.walkthrough: The Liberals merged into the Liberal Democrats in 1988, hence 'Old'.
explanation.definitionFit: The scales are one of the twelve zodiac signs, the seventh in the cycle.

clue.text: Put out statement in flier

parts.note: put out means annoyed or angry
a bill is a statement of money owed

explanation.surface: Someone issues a statement printed in a leaflet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flier' is a bird, not a leaflet as the surface suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: A finch whose bill tips cross over is a bird, and birds are fliers.

clue.text: Disapproving cry from New Zealanders having little time for a stick-in-the-mud?

parts.note: Wellington, the New Zealand capital, here stands for its people
boo is a cry of disapproval
T is a short form of time

explanation.surface: New Zealanders jeer a dull conservative, sparing little time for them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stick-in-the-mud' means a dull person, but read literally it is a boot that gets stuck in the mud.
explanation.definitionFit: A rubber knee-high boot worn in wet fields often sticks fast in mud, hence the cryptic description.

clue.text: Chicken ahead of cow, leader's top

indicators.note: in a down clue ahead of means placed above, so first

parts.note: chicken and yellow both mean cowardly
a Jersey is a breed of dairy cow

explanation.surface: A chicken running ahead of a cow becomes the farmyard leader.
explanation.walkthrough: The leader of the Tour de France cycle race wears a yellow top.
explanation.definitionFit: The shirt worn by the overall leader in the Tour de France is that leader's top.

clue.text: Con party eccentric

parts.note: to screw someone is slang for to cheat or con them
a ball is a formal dance party

explanation.surface: A trickster at a party behaves oddly.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for an oddball or crank, a person of strange behaviour.

clue.text: Passage into India is legendary

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the run of words India is legendary

explanation.surface: A route into India is the stuff of legend.
explanation.definitionFit: A walkway between rows of seats or shelves is a passage.

clue.text: In the role of an old king, Canute ultimately perceptive

parts.note: as means in the role of, as in acting as chairman
Tut is short for Tutankhamun, the boy pharaoh of ancient Egypt

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of Canute

explanation.surface: Acting as the old king Canute, who famously could not stop the tide, someone proves wise in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: Canute is a red herring for the king: only his last letter is used.
explanation.definitionFit: Shrewd and quick to see how things stand, which is what being perceptive means.

clue.text: First spin in cricket match getting shot of a batsman

parts.note: a Test is an international cricket match
a drive is a forward stroke played by a batsman in cricket

explanation.surface: A spin bowler on debut in a cricket match gets rid of a batsman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spin' suggests spin bowling, but it is a drive in a car.
explanation.definitionFit: A trial run in a car before buying it is a first spin behind the wheel.

clue.text: Boxed in turn, a kid beaten remains flattened

indicators.note: the anagram is boxed inside the word for turn

parts.note: a roll is a turning over, as in a roll of an aircraft

indicators.note: beaten means knocked about, so the letters of a kid are rearranged

explanation.surface: A young goat caught in a spin is beaten and left flat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'remains' is a noun here, the leftover body, not a verb meaning stays.
explanation.definitionFit: Animals killed by traffic and squashed on the tarmac are remains flattened on the road.

clue.text: One performing as a woman putting burden on man

indicators.note: in a down clue on means placed above the next piece

parts.note: a drag is a burden or tiresome thing
a queen is a chess piece, and chess pieces are called men

explanation.surface: Someone loads a burden onto a man.
explanation.definitionFit: A male entertainer who performs dressed in exaggerated women's clothing is one performing as a woman.

clue.text: Intimate relationship's beginning, boy wearing ring

indicators.note: the ring word is worn round the other pieces, enclosing them

parts.note: a peal is a ringing of bells

indicators.note: the beginning of the word relationship is its first letter

parts.note: a son is a boy

explanation.surface: An intimate relationship starts with a boy wearing a ring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ring' looks like a piece of jewellery; it is the sound of bells.
explanation.definitionFit: Private and close, as in a personal matter, an intimate one.

clue.text: Cool to pour in wine

indicators.note: the word for pour goes in the word for wine

parts.note: red is short for red wine
to serve drinks is to pour them

explanation.surface: Instructions for chilling something before pouring it into wine.
explanation.definitionFit: A reserved person is cool and distant in manner.

clue.text: In expression of amazement, nothing but delight

indicators.note: the word for nothing but goes in the exclamation

parts.note: wow is an exclamation of amazement
nothing but means all, as in nothing but skin and bones

explanation.surface: An amazed cry expressing pure joy.
explanation.definitionFit: To revel or bask in something, as in wallowing in praise, is to take great pleasure in it.

clue.text: Completely gone — as are cherries?

definitions.meaning: slang for extremely drunk or high on drugs
cherries have their pits removed for cooking

explanation.definitionFit: Slang for very intoxicated, and also with pits removed, as prepared cherries are.

clue.text: Ancient kingdom largely evacuated, charity recalled

indicators.note: an evacuated word has had its insides emptied, leaving only its first and last letters
recalled means called back, so the word for charity runs backwards

parts.note: aid is charitable help

explanation.surface: A mostly emptied old realm calls back its charity workers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'evacuated' leaves LY of 'largely'; 'recalled' turns AID into DIA.
explanation.definitionFit: An ancient realm in Asia Minor, ruled by Croesus, so an old kingdom.

clue.text: Where junk may be all over the shop

definitions.meaning: a junk is a Chinese sailing ship, which may be out on the ocean
all over the shop means confused or disorganised

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means out on the ocean, where a ship sails, and figuratively bewildered or lost.

clue.text: Device for drawing level after a few games

indicators.note: the word for level comes after the word for games

parts.note: a set in tennis is made up of several games
square means level, as in all square

explanation.surface: A piece of drawing kit used to level things after playing a few games.
explanation.definitionFit: A triangular plate for drawing right angles and lines is a technical drawing instrument.

clue.text: Set aside first of logs in piles

indicators.note: the picked letter goes in the word for piles

parts.note: piles means a great deal, a lot

indicators.note: first of picks out the opening letter of logs

explanation.surface: Someone puts aside the first of the logs from the woodpiles.
explanation.definitionFit: To allocate or assign something for a purpose is to set it aside.

clue.text: Numbing feeling, doctors end endless pain

indicators.note: doctors as a verb means tampers with, so the following letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Doctors bring an end to unending pain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' looks like an instruction to cut a letter, but it is part of the anagram as written.
explanation.definitionFit: The tingling sensation in a limb that has gone numb is a numbing feeling.

clue.text: Last part in document, thorough

indicators.note: the last part goes in the word for document

parts.note: a deed is a legal document
the tail is the last part of something

explanation.surface: The final section of a document is comprehensive.
explanation.definitionFit: Full of particulars and covering every point, a thorough account.

clue.text: Out to lunch — like some fruit?

definitions.meaning: slang for crazy or not all there
some fruit tastes of or is full of nuts

explanation.definitionFit: Slang for crazy, and also tasting of or full of nuts, like some fruit cakes.
